title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Sum Divisible by K
statement: In one operation you pick any index `i` of the integer array `nums` and lower `nums[i]` by `1`; you may do this as many times as you like, on any indices. Return the fewest operations after which the sum of `nums` is a multiple of `k` (a sum of `0` counts as a multiple).
notes:
## Intuition

Whichever element an operation touches, the sum of `nums` drops by exactly 1, so only the sum matters. Starting from `sum` and stepping down one at a time, the first multiple of `k` reached is `sum - sum % k`, which takes `sum % k` steps. No element ever has to go negative, because `sum % k` is never more than `sum`. Simulating the steps one by one (the brute force) gives the same count, just more slowly.

## Approach

1. Add up every `num` of `nums` into `sum`.
2. Return `sum % k`, the distance down to the nearest multiple of `k`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 9, 7]`, `k = 5`. The loop builds `sum` as 3, then 12, then 19. Since `19 % 5 = 4`, four operations bring the sum to 15, a multiple of 5 (for example by lowering 9 to 5). The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) to add up the array.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Operations only lower values, so the answer is `sum % k`, not the distance to the closest multiple in either direction.
- When `sum` is already a multiple of `k` (including when `k = 1`), the answer is `0`.
- There is no need to choose which elements to lower: any choice gives the same sum.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sum` | total of all values in `nums` |
| `num` | the element being added |

narration.1: Every operation lowers the array's sum by exactly 1, whichever element it changes, so only the sum matters.
narration.2: sum will hold the total of nums.
narration.4: Add it to the running total.
narration.5: Now sum is the total before any operation.
narration.6: Stepping down from sum, the first multiple of k is sum - sum % k, so sum % k operations are needed and enough.
